subject.title: Keep Windows Companion aligned with current OpenClaw stable and beta releases

question: Should the Companion wait for the upstream startup-migration regression to be fixed before promoting 2026.7.1, or intentionally ship that stable pin with failed setup E2E?
rationale: The existing drift policy favors current stable, but repository policy requires successful real setup proof; accepting a known fresh-install failure is a release decision automation cannot make safely.

options.title: Require green setup proof
options.body: Keep the draft update blocked until the upstream regression is fixed and fresh-install plus upgrade proof succeeds, then promote the fixed stable promptly.

options.title: Ship the known failure
options.body: Promote 2026.7.1 now and explicitly accept that some fresh Companion installs may fail during gateway startup.

options.title: Skip to the next fixed stable
options.body: Retain 2026.6.11 until a later stable contains the upstream fix, then validate and promote that version instead of 2026.7.1.

recommendation.title: Require green setup proof
recommendation.body: Keep the draft update blocked until the upstream regression is fixed and fresh-install plus upgrade proof succeeds, then promote the fixed stable promptly.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged setup stabilization work makes shanselman the strongest available human routing candidate for the release-safety choice.
